method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: The only avenue that reaches both sheets is Broadway (Ave J), and it does so at the corner where they meet: sheet 84's east margin prints '85' and sheet 93's west margin prints '92', so sheet 84 (39TH-42ND ST, Avenues G-J) and sheet 93 (42ND-46TH ST, Avenues J-M) are diagonal neighbours whose only common corridor is Broadway. PRINTED NAME. Sheet 84 letters 'AVE. J OR BROADWAY' vertically in the roadway east of block column 219/220/221, with 150' printed as the roadway width and a 10 in. W. PIPE dashed main running down it. Sheet 93 letters 'BROADWAY' and 'AVE. J OR' in the roadway west of block column 163/164, also with 150'. ADDRESS RUNS. On sheet 84 the block column immediately WEST of the line carries the 900 block on every cross street - '901 903 905 907 909 911 913 915 917 919 921 923' / '902 ... 924' along 40TH, 41ST and 42ND ST - and its Broadway frontage reads 3902-3928 (39th-40th block), i.e. the west side of Broadway. On sheet 93 the block column immediately EAST of the line carries the 1000 block - '1001 1003 1005 ... 1023' / '1002 ... 1024' along 43RD, 44TH and 45TH ST - and its Broadway frontage reads 4313-4327 (43rd-44th) and 4401-4417 (44th-45th), i.e. the east side of Broadway. The line is therefore the 900/1000 boundary, read independently from each sheet. ONE BLOCK WEST is excluded: on sheet 84 that corridor is lettered 'AVE. I OR SEALY' (faces 2068.8/2268.3, centre 2168.6) and is the 800/900 boundary. ONE BLOCK EAST is excluded: on sheet 93 that corridor is lettered 'AVENUE K' (faces 1067.8/1275.2, centre 1171.5) and is the 1000/1100 boundary. HOW THE COORDINATE WAS OBTAINED (read this before using the control). Neither sheet draws the whole of Broadway. Sheet 84's paper ends inside the roadway at native ~3256 and shows only Broadway's WEST face, measured at native 3060.4; sheet 93's paper begins inside the roadway at native ~42 and shows only Broadway's EAST face, measured at native 279.9. No single drawn line therefore appears on both sheets, so the reported coordinate is the corridor CENTRELINE, obtained by offsetting each measured face by half of Broadway's drawn width. Broadway is drawn compressed - sheet 69 annotates it 'AVE. J OR BROADWAY 150 ft wide' yet draws it only ~301 px, where a 70 ft avenue on the same plate is ~209 px - so its drawn width was measured on the three plates that show both faces: sheet 69 (2004.9/2305.0 = 300.1, 2009.5/2309.4 = 299.9, 2008.8/2310.5 = 301.8 in its three block rows), sheet 77 (1000.5/1302.4 = 301.9) and sheet 56 (1001.7/1304.1 = 302.4). Mean 301.2 px, sd 1.1, half-width 150.6 +/- 0.6 px. a_native = 3060.4 + 150.6 = 3211.0 (still inside sheet 84's paper, ~45 px from its edge); b_native = 279.9 - 150.6 = 129.3 (inside sheet 93's paper). CONSISTENCY CHECK: the distance from the nearest lettered avenue to the derived Broadway centre comes out the same on both sheets - 3211.0 - 2168.6 (Ave I, sheet 84) = 1042.4 px and 1171.5 (Ave K, sheet 93) - 129.3 = 1042.2 px - and the two sheets' block depths agree (792.1 px for the I-J column on 84, 787.9 px for the J-K column on 93), so both coordinates describe the same corridor at the same plate scale. CANDIDATES REJECTED: sheet 84's 2586/1569/552 and sheet 93's 1747/722/2772 all fall inside block interiors; none is within 240 px of an avenue centre on its sheet. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY ~3 px: Broadway's west face on sheet 84 drifts from 3052.8 in its top block row to 3061.2 in its bottom one (slight plate skew), and the half-width constant is good to ~0.6 px; a one-block error would be ~1042 px.
